\chapter{Come In, Here You Are}
\label{ch:hi-come-in}
\hlchaptermodality{115}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can welcome a guest in, offer something, answer by all means, and say no politely.}

Complete HI-R115-second-pass-courtesy: courtesies and reactions, from cold.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[āie]{\hi{आइए} (āie) — please come (in)}

\label{lesson:HI-C115-aie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for good wishes, then the Hindi for an invitation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{आइए}}
\textbf{\hi{आइए}} (\emph{āie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please come\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}come in\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{आना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful \textbf{-\hi{इए}}. \textbf{\hi{आइए}, \hi{आइए}!} — doubled, it is a warm welcome at the door.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A welcome at the door.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āie, āie!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for good wishes, then the Hindi for an invitation, then say \emph{āie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{आइए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please come (in)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[padhārie]{\hi{पधारिए} (padhārie) — please come (formal)}

\label{lesson:HI-C115-padharie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an invitation, then the Hindi for please come in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पधारिए}}
\textbf{\hi{पधारिए}} (\emph{padhārie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please come\textquotedblright{}, in its most formal, honouring form.

The everyday \emph{āie} comes first in this chapter; \textbf{\hi{पधारिए}} is what you say to an honoured guest.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second welcome, for an honoured guest.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padhārie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padhārie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{padhārie}, then \emph{āie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an invitation, then the Hindi for please come in, then say \emph{padhārie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पधारिए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please come (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[lījie]{\hi{लीजिए} (lījie) — please take; here you are}

\label{lesson:HI-C115-lijie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for please come in, then the Hindi for please come, formally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लीजिए}}
\textbf{\hi{लीजिए}} (\emph{lījie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please take\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}here you are\textquotedblright{}, as you hand something over.

It is \textbf{\hi{लेना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful ending of \textbf{\hi{बोलिए}}. \textbf{\hi{चाय} \hi{लीजिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}have some tea\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An offer as you hand it over.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lījie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lījie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cāy lījie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for please come in, then the Hindi for please come, formally, then say \emph{lījie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{लीजिए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please take; here you are\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[śauq se]{\hi{शौक़} \hi{से} (śauq se) — by all means, gladly}

\label{lesson:HI-C115-shauqse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for please come, formally, then the Hindi for here you are.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{शौक़} \hi{से}}
\textbf{\hi{शौक़} \hi{से}} (\emph{śauq se}) — \textquotedblleft{}by all means\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}gladly\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}with pleasure\textquotedblright{}.

The answer when someone asks if they may: \textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{मैं} \hi{बैठ} \hi{सकता} \hi{हूँ}? — \hi{शौक़} \hi{से}!}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A generous yes.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śauq se}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śauq se}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{śauq se!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for please come, formally, then the Hindi for here you are, then say \emph{śauq se} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{शौक़} \hi{से} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}By all means, gladly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[jī nahīṁ]{\hi{जी} \hi{नहीं} (jī nahīṁ) — no, politely}

\label{lesson:HI-C115-jinahin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for here you are, then the Hindi for by all means.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जी} \hi{नहीं}}
\textbf{\hi{जी} \hi{नहीं}} (\emph{jī nahīṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}no\textquotedblright{}, said politely.

It pairs with the \textbf{\hi{जी} \hi{हाँ}} you know: \textbf{\hi{जी}} makes either answer respectful.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Come in, please come, here you are, by all means, and a polite no.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jī nahīṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jī nahīṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jī nahīṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for here you are, then the Hindi for by all means, then say \emph{jī nahīṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{जी} \hi{नहीं} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}No, politely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{A visit, start to finish — a second pass}

\label{lesson:HI-R115-second-pass-courtesy}



\begin{quote}
A guest is at your door. Welcome them in, and hand them a cup of tea.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the respectful ending}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{from} \\
\midrule
\emph{āie} & come \\
\textbf{\hi{लीजिए}} & take \\
\textbf{\hi{पधारिए}} & arrive, formally \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

One ending turns a verb into a polite request, as it did for \textbf{\hi{बोलिए}}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item you bumped into someone: beg their pardon; they answer \textquotedblleft{}no problem\textquotedblright{}
  \item congratulate a friend; then send them good wishes
  \item thank someone for an invitation
  \item a guest asks to sit: say \textquotedblleft{}by all means\textquotedblright{}; offered more food, say a polite no
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An apology? (\textbf{\hi{माफ़ी}}.) No problem? (\textbf{\hi{कोई} \hi{बात} \hi{नहीं}}.) Congratulations? (\textbf{\hi{बधाई}}.) Good wishes? (\textbf{\hi{शुभकामनाएँ}}.) An invitation? (\textbf{\hi{निमंत्रण}}.) Come in? (\emph{āie}.) Please come, formally? (\textbf{\hi{पधारिए}}.) Here you are? (\textbf{\hi{लीजिए}}.) By all means? (\textbf{\hi{शौक़} \hi{से}}.) A polite no? (\textbf{\hi{जी} \hi{नहीं}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Reacting and answering — a second pass}

\label{lesson:HI-R115-second-pass-reactions}



\begin{quote}
Someone gives an answer. Tell them it is right; then tell them it is wrong.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: two words you already had, joined}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{answer} & \textbf{built from} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\hi{कुछ} \hi{नहीं}} & something + not \\
\textbf{\hi{अभी} \hi{नहीं}} & right now + not \\
\textbf{\hi{सच} \hi{में}?} & truth + in \\
\textbf{\hi{वही}} & that + exactly \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Most short answers are two small words you already own, put side by side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item react to surprising news: oh, really?
  \item ask if someone is sure; answer \textquotedblleft{}definitely\textquotedblright{}
  \item asked what happened, say nothing; asked if you have finished, say not yet
  \item say that's enough; say \textquotedblleft{}that's the one\textquotedblright{}; say maybe
  \item answer a request with \textquotedblleft{}by all means\textquotedblright{}, then with a polite no
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Right? (\textbf{\hi{सही}}.) Wrong? (\textbf{\hi{ग़लत}}.) Sure? (\textbf{\hi{पक्का}}.) Really? (\textbf{\hi{सच} \hi{में}?}) Oh? (\textbf{\hi{अरे}}.) Nothing? (\textbf{\hi{कुछ} \hi{नहीं}}.) Not yet? (\textbf{\hi{अभी} \hi{नहीं}}.) Enough? (\textbf{\hi{काफ़ी}}.) That very one? (\textbf{\hi{वही}}.) Maybe? (\textbf{\hi{हो} \hi{सकता} \hi{है}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
